supporting_observations.claim: Repeated HTTPS CONNECT attempts from WS-BCARTER-01 to update.chartmate-imaging.net:443 are visible from 13:38 through 14:08 UTC, at roughly five-minute intervals. The 13:43 and 13:52 attempts returned proxy statuses 407 and 502; the other listed attempts returned 200.

The outbound proxy connections are attributed to cmupdate.exe running as ben.carter: process creation is recorded at 13:37:57, and network events for that image map to the proxy connections, including at 13:38, 13:47, 13:52, 13:58, 14:03, and 14:08.

The application name and approximately five-minute check pattern are consistent with the documented ChartMate updater, but the evidence shows the executable at a user AppData path and the destination as update.chartmate-imaging.net; the inventory instead documents a Program Files path and update.chartmate-imaging.com. The identity of this binary and endpoint as the approved updater is therefore not verified by the available records.

A file creation event for cmupdate.exe at the same AppData path was logged seconds after the process started. This could be related to updater behavior, but the record alone does not establish the file's origin or legitimacy.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT destinations and outcomes, but successful tunnels do not expose the encrypted application content in these records (for example, T015-00110 and T015-00281).

The recorded workstation network events identify connections to the internal proxy on port 8080, not the final external destination IP or the remote server's TLS certificate (for example, T015-00113 and T015-00284).
The supplied records do not provide a binary hash, signature validation, file provenance, or updater logs for the observed cmupdate.exe.
claims_not_established: Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is an authorized ChartMate endpoint or is controlled by the legitimate vendor.
Whether the observed AppData cmupdate.exe is authentic ChartMate software, and why it differs from the inventory's documented path.
Whether the repeated connections transferred any content beyond what can be inferred from the proxy tunnel records.
Whether the 13:30–13:37 portion of the alert window contained the same activity; no corresponding ChartMate proxy records are supplied for that portion.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify the canonical ChartMate update hostname and whether the .net endpoint is approved; confirm with the vendor or the organization's software/change records.
Acquire the observed executable and determine its SHA-256 hash, Authenticode signature, file provenance, and any updater logs explaining its AppData location and the file creation event.
Collect proxy or endpoint telemetry that identifies the external destination IP and TLS certificate for the successful connections, and preserve any available full proxy logs for the alert window.
unrelated_findings: At 13:54 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON. This is outside the alerted HTTPS activity and should be reviewed separately; the supplied records do not establish what resource was accessed or whether this was malicious. (T015-00253, T015-00255, T015-00257)
